title: Report the answer and its limits
summary: A useful report states the question, result, method and limits. Readers should be able to check where the answer came from.
introduction: A useful report states the question, result, method and limits. Readers should be able to check where the answer came from. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain report the answer and its limits
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A useful report states the question, result, method and limits. Readers should be able to check where the answer came from.

blocks.code:
Question: which type was borrowed most this week?
Sample: 4 fictional borrowing events
Result: story had 2 events; science and poetry had 1 each
Limit: one tiny week does not describe the whole year
blocks.title: Report the answer and its limits

blocks.text: The report answers its own question without stretching the evidence. The event count makes the small sample clear.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Add a sentence explaining what data could help compare several weeks.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not hide missing data or small samples behind a confident title.
For more detail later, use this [Data Science further reading](https://www.openintro.org/book/ims/).

seo.title: Data Science: Report the answer and its limits
seo.description: Learn about report the answer and its limits in Data Science. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
